- Large irregular necrotic/brown areas covering most of the leaf
- Complete tissue collapse with holes where tissue has disintegrated
- Yellowing/chlorosis in the remaining green areas
- Rapid tissue breakdown suggesting aggressive disease progression

The large, irregular brown necrotic lesions with tissue collapse suggest Late Blight. Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image is a microscopic view (sporangia), not a macro leaf symptom view. I'll rely on my visual analysis of the test image.

**Analysis summary:**
- Large, irregular brown necrotic lesions covering most of the leaf
- Complete tissue collapse creating holes where tissue has disintegrated
- Yellowing/chlorosis at the margins of green tissue
- No concentric ring pattern (ruling out Early Blight)
- No gray fuzzy growth visible (ruling out Gray Mold)
- Rapid, aggressive tissue destruction consistent with Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans) in advanced stages

The irregular water-soaked-to-brown necrosis spreading rapidly across the leaf, with complete tissue breakdown, is classic Late Blight progression.
